from_speaker: A.I. is not even good, reliable software
resembles the death of the art of technology
ADDS to the cognitive load of the user by requiring them to be ever-vigilant
our_interpretation: This sentence bundles five or six value judgments into one rhetorical line. Some are normative ('good', 'death of the art of technology'). Some are conceptual ('by definition', 'by design'). None comes with a measure, a comparator, a period, or a named party.
'Financially ruinous' does not say for whom: AI companies, investors, customers, or the economy.
'Adds to cognitive load' names no baseline. Is it compared with doing the task without AI, or with ideal software? Needing vigilance does not by itself fix the net workload.

Any test would rest on measures, comparators and periods the evaluator would have to invent, and the result would turn on those choices. Earlier reviewers already objected to this on fairness grounds. So the claim is treated as not adjudicable.
criteria.support_condition: None can be stated fairly. The sentence names no measure that evidence could meet.
criteria.contradiction_condition: None can be stated fairly. The sentence names no measure that evidence could fail.
